text.p: Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA surged on Tuesday, boosted by signs Brazil would sell off a big state-run company.

Telebras was up 3-1/2 to 118-3/8 in late morning, close to a 12-month high. Volume was 1.2 million American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), putting the company among the most active on the New York Stock Exchange.
Traders said Telebras was helped by the start of the auction of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).

The sale had been blocked by repeated court orders sought by opponents. The auction is considered a crucial step forward in Brazil's efforts to sell off its state-run companies and open its economy to private firms, including the telephone sector.
"There have been concerns about the auction on CVRD, the whole privatization issue," a trader said. "This is more related to the privatization issue than anything else."

Among European shares, Italian footware and apparel company Fila Holdings SpA fell 5-1/4, or 11.44 percent, to 40-5/8 after the company reported first quarter earnings of $1.22 per ADR against $1.08 for the same period a year before.
The ADRs were the largest percentage loser on the New York Stock Exchange.
Fila's chief executive said the results reflected softness in U.S. markets and momentum outside the United States. Goldman Sachs cut its rating for the ADRs to market perform from outperform.
British Petroleum Co Plc rose 4-3/4 to 143-3/4 after it reported first quarter results well above market forecasts.
Japanese blue chips rose following an overnight rally in Tokyo. Toyota Motor Co was up 3-1/8 to 64 and Sony Corp rose 1-5/8 to 76-1/4.
Advancers led decliners 258 to 187 among 806 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.67 percent and volume was 35 million shares.
